reason: The text contains explicit instances of the Israelites complaining against their leaders. Specifically: (1) 'וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל־ מֹשֶׁה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹן כֹּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל' - 'all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron'; (2) The people express their discontent, saying they would have preferred to die in Egypt or the wilderness rather than enter Canaan; (3) God explicitly references 'תְּלֻנּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל' - 'the complaints of the children of Israel which they murmur against me.' The passage centers on the Israelites' rebellion and complaints directed at Moses and Aaron for bringing them into danger.
